description: Initial Spanish-language YouTube corpus candidates for native-speech retrieval experiments.

sections.name: Language learning and language-focused content
sections.description: Clear native Spanish with strong linguistic or pedagogical value; useful for high-quality baseline examples.

channels.name: Easy Spanish
channels.description: One of the strongest starting points: native speakers discussing everyday topics in street interviews and conversations, with learner-oriented presentation and unusually useful subtitle material.

channels.name: Dreaming Spanish
channels.description: A very large learner-oriented corpus built around comprehensible input. Speakers are native and the material spans slow beginner speech through substantially more natural conversational Spanish.

channels.name: Spanish After Hours
channels.description: Clear native European Spanish with stories, explanations and conversational material. Particularly useful for intermediate vocabulary and clean baseline retrieval examples.

channels.name: Linguriosa
channels.description: Spanish-language linguistic outreach covering words, expressions, etymology, phonetics, grammar and register. Especially valuable because the content itself frequently discusses language usage.

sections.name: Travel and real-world interaction
sections.description: Narration mixed with spontaneous conversations and speech recorded in real situations.

channels.name: Luisito Comunica
channels.description: A strong real-world corpus: Mexican narration combined with spontaneous interactions with people across many countries and situations.

channels.name: Alan por el mundo
channels.description: Travel content combining clear Mexican narration with natural conversations and practical real-world situations.

sections.name: Long-form conversation and contemporary informal speech
sections.description: High-volume unscripted or semi-structured speech, useful for colloquialisms, discourse markers and phrase retrieval.

channels.name: The Wild Project
channels.description: Large quantities of natural European Spanish conversation. Particularly useful for colloquialisms, discourse markers and longer conversational constructions.

channels.name: Ter
channels.description: Contemporary, informal European Spanish around culture and humour. Useful as a less textbook-like source of modern vocabulary and expressive language.

channels.name: La Ruina
channels.description: Live comedy built around people telling personal stories. Valuable for spontaneous storytelling, conversational phrasing and audience interaction.

sections.name: Argentina and Rioplatense Spanish
sections.description: A deliberately strong Argentine component for colloquial vocabulary and constructions that generic pan-Hispanic corpora often underrepresent.

channels.name: Gelatina
channels.description: Long conversational programs with very natural contemporary Rioplatense Spanish, mixing politics, culture, humour, interviews and everyday discussion.

channels.name: OLGA
channels.description: High-volume casual Argentine conversation with multiple speakers, celebrities and humour. Particularly attractive for colloquial expressions and naturally occurring phrase variants.

channels.name: LUZU TV
channels.description: A large source of casual contemporary Argentine speech, with long multi-speaker programs and substantial coverage of everyday conversational language.

channels.name: BLENDER
channels.description: Contemporary Argentine conversational content and streaming, useful for informal vocabulary, humour and current spoken usage.

channels.name: Filo News
channels.description: Argentine journalism and interviews. The longer interview material is especially useful for natural but comparatively well-structured speech.

channels.name: Televisión Pública
channels.description: Institutional Argentine television with interviews, cultural programming and news; useful as a relatively stable source of high-quality Argentine Spanish.

channels.name: Canal Encuentro
channels.description: Argentine documentary and educational programming. More formal than streaming channels, but strong for high-quality speech, interviews and broad topical vocabulary.

channels.name: Trasnoche Paranormal
channels.description: Long-form Argentine conversation and storytelling. The subject matter is niche, but the format provides many hours of naturally flowing speech.

sections.name: Documentary, journalism and institutional media
sections.description: Stable, large archives with clean audio, interviews and a more formal register.

channels.name: VICE en Español
channels.description: Documentaries and interviews spanning culture, travel, nightlife, social issues and street-level reporting, including productions from several Spanish-speaking countries.

channels.name: DW Español
channels.description: A large institutional archive with strong audio quality, documentaries and interviews. Useful for a cleaner and more formal complement to casual-speech channels.

channels.name: BBC News Mundo
channels.description: Clear journalistic Spanish plus interviews with speakers from many countries, giving broad regional and topical coverage.

channels.name: RTVE
channels.description: Spanish public broadcasting material covering interviews, documentaries, culture, travel, science and language. Useful for stable, professionally produced European Spanish.

sections.name: Science and educational narration
sections.description: Clearer, more structured native speech useful for educated general vocabulary and comparison against conversational data.

channels.name: QuantumFracture
channels.description: Clear European Spanish science communication and narration. Useful for precise, educated vocabulary and clean speech.

sections.name: Scripted comedy and interviews
sections.description: Useful for everyday situational dialogue and longer structured personal conversations.

channels.name: EnchufeTV
channels.description: Scripted comedy with everyday situational dialogue. Although less spontaneous than interviews or podcasts, it can provide concise and highly contextualized examples.

channels.name: Yordi Rosado
channels.description: Long Mexican interviews that provide substantial amounts of natural, structured conversational speech and personal storytelling.
